questions.question: In the Azure Shared Responsibility Model, which task is ALWAYS the customer's responsibility, regardless of whether they use IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS?
options: Patching the host operating system underneath their VMs
Managing identity, accounts, and access controls for users of the workload
Maintaining the physical security of the datacenter
Configuring the underlying network fabric between Azure regions
questions.explanation: Identity and access management (who can sign in, what they can do) is always the customer's job across IaaS/PaaS/SaaS. Host OS patching is Microsoft's job in PaaS/SaaS but the customer's in IaaS — so it varies. Datacenter physical security and the network fabric are always Microsoft.

questions.question: An app needs to store any size of arbitrary file (images, videos, parquet, JSON) accessed via HTTPS REST API with object semantics — NOT a POSIX filesystem, NOT a block device. The service should expose Hot / Cool / Cold / Archive tiers and 11-nines durability. Which Azure service?
options: Azure Managed Disks — block storage attached to a VM, not object
Azure Files — managed SMB / NFS file shares, not object
Azure Blob Storage — managed object storage with Hot/Cool/Cold/Archive tiers, REST API, 11 nines durability
Azure Table Storage — NoSQL key-value, not object-blob
questions.explanation: Azure Blob Storage is optimized for storing massive amounts of unstructured data like images, videos, backups, and logs. It supports hot, cool, and archive access tiers.

questions.question: A workload requires the LOWEST possible latency between two VMs and tolerance for a single datacenter failure within the same metro area. Which Azure deployment best fits these constraints?
options: Deploy both VMs in the same Availability Zone within one Region
Deploy the VMs in two different Availability Zones within the same Region
Deploy the VMs in two paired Regions
Deploy the VMs in two different Resource Groups within one Subscription
questions.explanation: Two AZs in one Region give physical isolation (separate datacenters, independent power/network) with sub-millisecond inter-zone latency — the canonical "HA + low latency" trade. Same AZ doesn't survive a datacenter failure. Paired Regions introduce ~tens of ms latency. Resource Groups are management constructs, not a placement boundary.

questions.question: A storage account is configured with Geo-Zone-Redundant Storage (GZRS). How many copies of the data exist, and where?
options: 3 copies, all within a single datacenter in the primary region
3 copies across 3 zones in the primary region only
6 copies: 3 across zones in the primary region and 3 in a single datacenter in the paired region
6 copies across 3 zones in both the primary and the paired region
questions.explanation: GZRS = ZRS in the primary region (3 copies, one per zone) + LRS in the paired region (3 copies in one datacenter). 6 total. The fourth option describes a hypothetical "GZRS with zonal copies in the paired region" which Azure does not offer (the paired region is LRS, not ZRS, in GZRS).

questions.question: Which cloud model gives you the most control over the underlying infrastructure?
options: SaaS
FaaS
PaaS
IaaS
questions.explanation: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) provides VMs, storage, and networking — you control the OS, runtime, and applications. PaaS and SaaS abstract more of the infrastructure.

questions.question: An organisation's M365 users sign in with email + password to access SharePoint, Teams, Outlook, AND third-party SaaS apps via SAML/OIDC federation. The user directory + MFA + SSO + B2B Guest invites all live in one Microsoft cloud product. Which one?
options: On-premises AD — different product (on-prem directory service)
VM management — unrelated
Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) — cloud identity + auth + SSO + MFA + B2B/B2C
Azure DNS — DNS service, not identity
questions.explanation: Azure Active Directory (now Microsoft Entra ID) is a cloud-based IAM service providing authentication, single sign-on (SSO), multi-factor authentication, and conditional access.

questions.question: What is the Azure pricing benefit of using Reserved Virtual Machine Instances?
options: No benefit; pay-as-you-go is always cheaper
50% discount with no commitment
Free for the first year
Up to 72% savings vs pay-as-you-go for 1 or 3-year commitments
questions.explanation: Azure Reserved VM Instances provide up to 72% cost savings compared to pay-as-you-go pricing when you commit to 1 or 3 years for predictable workloads.

questions.question: Every action against Azure resources — create, read, update, delete — goes through ONE control plane that processes the request, enforces RBAC, applies policies, and orchestrates the underlying resource providers. Templates (Bicep / ARM JSON) compile against this same control plane. Which Azure service is this?
options: Physical hardware-management server tool — not Azure-relevant
Azure Backup service — backup workloads only
Azure Resource Manager (ARM) — the unified control plane for all Azure resource CRUD, RBAC, policy, and ARM templates
Antivirus solution — security agent, not the control plane
questions.explanation: ARM is the management layer for Azure. All Azure management tools (portal, CLI, PowerShell, SDKs) go through ARM. It enables RBAC, tagging, locks, and template-based deployments.

questions.question: What is a benefit of the public cloud over on-premises infrastructure?
options: No need for internet connectivity
Capital expenditure (CapEx) model
Eliminates capital expenditure.
Always cheaper
questions.explanation: Cloud shifts IT spending from CapEx (upfront hardware) to OpEx (pay-as-you-go). You don't buy servers; you pay for services consumed. shifts to operational expenditure (OpEx)

questions.question: Which Azure service provides serverless code execution?
options: Azure Container Instances
Azure Functions
Azure Virtual Machines
Azure App Service
questions.explanation: Azure Functions is a serverless compute service. You write event-driven code and pay only for execution time. No server management required.

questions.question: A CISO wants ONE managed service that delivers: (a) security-posture score across all Azure subscriptions, (b) threat detection on VMs / SQL / Storage / containers, (c) regulatory-compliance dashboards (PCI-DSS, ISO, NIST) across Azure + on-prem + AWS / GCP via Azure Arc. Which Azure service?
options: Identity-only product (e.g., Azure AD Identity Protection) — narrower than the multi-workload posture service described
Microsoft Defender for Cloud (formerly Azure Security Center / Azure Defender) — unified posture + threat protection across Azure, on-prem, AWS, GCP
VM-only antivirus product — narrower than 'workload + multi-cloud + posture'
Standalone firewall service — narrower than the unified posture/threat platform
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud provides unified security management and advanced threat protection. It assesses security posture and detects threats across hybrid environments.

questions.question: An SLA document from Microsoft for Azure SQL Database lists '99.99% monthly availability'. The customer asks what this represents legally and operationally. Which is the correct definition?
options: A billing agreement — about payment terms, not service uptime
A 100% uptime guarantee — false; SLAs are never 100% and include service-credit terms for misses
A support contract — separate document (support plan tiers), not the SLA
A formal Microsoft commitment to a minimum service availability (e.g. 99.9% / 99.99%) — with credit remedies if missed
questions.explanation: Azure SLAs define the minimum uptime guarantees for each service. If Microsoft misses the SLA, customers receive service credits. Most services offer 99.9% to 99.99% SLAs.

questions.question: Which Azure tool lets you estimate costs before deploying resources?
options: Azure Monitor
Azure Cost Management
Azure Pricing Calculator
Azure Advisor
questions.explanation: The Azure Pricing Calculator lets you configure services and estimate monthly costs before deployment. Azure Cost Management analyzes actual spending.

questions.question: A central security team wants to enforce rules across hundreds of Azure subscriptions: 'no public IPs on storage accounts', 'all VMs must have backup', 'allowed regions = EU only'. Each rule must AUDIT existing resources AND DENY non-compliant new deployments at create-time. Which Azure service?
options: Azure Policy — declarative rules that audit compliance + actively deny non-compliant deployments + auto-remediate where applicable
Azure Monitor — telemetry only, no enforcement
Azure ARM Templates — deploy resources, not enforce rules
Azure AD identity governance — manages users, not resource configuration
questions.explanation: Azure Policy helps enforce rules (e.g., 'all VMs must use managed disks', 'resources must be tagged') and evaluates compliance of existing resources.

questions.question: A company runs mainframe + Active Directory on-prem AND modern apps in Azure, with bi-directional connectivity (AD sync, ExpressRoute, hybrid identity). Workloads can be moved between the two as needed. Which cloud deployment model is this?
options: Hybrid cloud — combination of on-prem / private + public cloud with integration between them
Private-only cloud — opposite of what's described
Multi-cloud — two public CSPs, not on-prem + Azure
Public-only cloud — opposite of what's described
questions.explanation: A hybrid cloud combines on-premises or private cloud infrastructure with public cloud services, allowing data and applications to move between environments.

questions.question: An admin opens an Azure portal blade that lists personalised recommendations grouped into FIVE categories: Reliability, Security, Performance, Cost, and Operational Excellence — each with concrete actions on specific resources. Which service is this?
options: Microsoft Defender for Cloud — security focus, not the 5-category general-recommendations blade
Azure Advisor — personalised free recommendations across Reliability, Security, Performance, Cost, Operational Excellence
Azure DNS — DNS management, unrelated
Azure Automation Account — runbooks, unrelated
questions.explanation: Azure Advisor analyzes your Azure usage and provides recommendations across 5 categories: reliability, security, performance, cost, and operational excellence.

questions.question: An ops team needs a SINGLE platform to ingest (a) Azure resource METRICS, (b) Azure resource and guest-OS LOGS, (c) Application Insights traces from apps, (d) on-prem servers via Azure Arc — and then to query, alert, and visualise across all of them. Which Azure service is this?
options: A deployment service like ARM — provisions resources, not telemetry
Azure Monitor — unified metrics + logs + traces + alerts + dashboards across Azure and on-prem (with Arc)
RBAC / Azure AD — manages user access, not telemetry
Azure Cost-alerts feature — billing, not telemetry
questions.explanation: Azure Monitor collects metrics and logs from resources, enables alerts and autoscale, and integrates with other tools like Application Insights and Log Analytics.

questions.question: A bank's CISO mandates that the SECOND factor of authentication must not be replayable from a stolen password alone. After entering the password, users must complete a SEPARATE verification (push notification, hardware token, biometric). Which security control is this?
options: Two consecutive passwords — both are knowledge factors, not multi-factor
Auto password rotation — security hygiene, not multi-factor authentication
Single sign-on — convenience across apps, not a stronger factor
Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) — two or more factors from DIFFERENT classes (know, have, are)
questions.explanation: MFA requires two or more verification factors: something you know (password), something you have (phone/authenticator app), or something you are (biometric). Significantly reduces breach risk.

questions.question: An admin groups related Azure resources (a web app + its SQL DB + key vault + storage) into a single container so they share a lifecycle, RBAC, and tag-based reporting. Deleting the container deletes the resources together. Which Azure construct?
options: A billing-account hierarchy — billing scope, not the deployable resource container
A VNet subnet — network isolation, not a generic resource container
An Azure Resource Group — logical container for resources with shared lifecycle + RBAC + policy
An Availability Zone — physical infrastructure scope, not a logical resource container
questions.explanation: Resource Groups are logical containers for organizing Azure resources. Resources in a group share lifecycle management — deploy, update, or delete them together.

questions.question: A team wants a MANAGED open-source relational database service for MySQL or PostgreSQL — pay-per-second compute + storage, automated backups, patching, HA option — with the open-source MySQL / PostgreSQL wire protocol (so existing drivers and apps work unchanged). Which Azure service?
options: Azure Cosmos DB — multi-model NoSQL; not MySQL/PostgreSQL wire-compatible
Azure SQL Database — managed SQL Server, not MySQL/PostgreSQL
Azure Database for MySQL / PostgreSQL — managed open-source MySQL and PostgreSQL services
Azure Cache for Redis — in-memory key-value, not relational
questions.explanation: Azure Database for MySQL and Azure Database for PostgreSQL are fully managed open-source database services. Azure SQL Database is for Microsoft SQL Server workloads.

questions.question: A dev team wants ONE platform for: Boards (Agile work-tracking), Repos (Git), Pipelines (CI/CD YAML), Test Plans (manual + exploratory), and Artifacts (package feeds). All integrate with each other and with Azure deployment. Which Microsoft offering?
options: Azure Networking — not a DevOps platform
Azure DevOps — Boards + Repos + Pipelines + Test Plans + Artifacts in one platform
Azure Virtual Machines — compute, not DevOps tooling
Azure Monitor — telemetry, not the DevOps toolchain
questions.explanation: Azure DevOps provides integrated tools: Boards (Agile planning), Repos (Git), Pipelines (CI/CD), Test Plans, and Artifacts (package management). Used end-to-end for software development lifecycle.

questions.question: A platform team wants to run containerised microservices on Kubernetes WITHOUT managing the control plane (etcd, API server, scheduler, controller-manager). They want to manage worker nodes (or use Virtual Nodes), declare services via kubectl, and integrate with Azure AD / ACR / Defender. Which Azure service?
options: Azure Virtual Machines — bare compute, no Kubernetes orchestration
Azure Functions — serverless functions, not full Kubernetes
Azure App Service — PaaS web hosting, not Kubernetes
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) — managed Kubernetes (free control plane, customer-managed node pools or Virtual Nodes)
questions.explanation: AKS is a managed Kubernetes service. Azure manages the control plane (API server, etcd) for free; you manage and pay for worker nodes. Integrates with Azure AD, Monitor, and Container Registry.

questions.question: A web tier behind an Azure Load Balancer experiences predictable daytime peaks. The team wants identical VM instances that AUTOMATICALLY add/remove based on CPU or schedule, using a shared image, with rolling-upgrade support. Which Azure compute construct?
options: Standalone VMs — managed individually, no built-in autoscale across a fleet
Azure VM Scale Sets — fleet of identical VMs with autoscale + rolling upgrades + integrated LB
AKS node pools — Kubernetes-only; question is about plain VMs
Azure Functions — serverless functions, not VM-based
questions.explanation: VM Scale Sets let you deploy and auto-scale a group of identical, load-balanced VMs. When demand increases, Scale Sets add VMs; when demand drops, they remove them — reducing manual management.

questions.question: A team wants to deploy a Node.js / .NET / Python web app to Azure WITHOUT managing OS / runtime / patching / scaling. Azure provides a managed PaaS that handles the runtime, SSL, autoscale, custom domains, deployment slots, and CI/CD from GitHub. Which Azure service?
options: An IaaS VM — customer manages OS and runtime, doesn't fit PaaS criteria
AKS — managed Kubernetes, still requires container expertise
Azure App Service — managed PaaS for web apps + APIs + mobile backends with runtime, SSL, scale, slots, CI/CD
Container Registry — image storage, not app hosting
questions.explanation: App Service supports .NET, Node.js, Python, PHP, Java, and containers. Azure manages patching, scaling, and infrastructure. You deploy code or containers and configure scaling rules.

questions.question: An app needs a globally distributed NoSQL database with: (a) sub-10 ms reads/writes anywhere, (b) multiple APIs (Core SQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table), (c) five-region multi-write, (d) SLAs on latency, throughput, availability, consistency. Which Azure service?
options: Azure SQL Data Warehouse / Synapse — analytical, not low-latency NoSQL
Azure Cosmos DB — globally distributed multi-model NoSQL with single-digit ms latency, multi-region writes, multiple APIs
Azure SQL Database — managed SQL Server, single-region primary
Azure Database for PostgreSQL — open-source RDBMS, not multi-model NoSQL
questions.explanation: Cosmos DB supports multiple APIs (SQL/Core, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table). Data is replicated globally with configurable consistency levels. SLA: 99.999% availability.

questions.question: An architect compares two Azure load balancers: (A) operates at TCP/UDP (Layer 4), routes by 5-tuple, terminates TCP, no HTTP awareness. (B) operates at HTTP/HTTPS (Layer 7), terminates TLS, routes by URL path / host header / cookie, integrates a WAF. Which mapping?
options: Load Balancer has built-in WAF — false; WAF is in Application Gateway
Application Gateway is internal-only — false; it has internet-facing + internal listeners
Azure Load Balancer = L4 (TCP/UDP); Azure Application Gateway = L7 (HTTP/S) with WAF + TLS termination + cookie affinity + URL-path routing
They are identical — false
questions.explanation: Azure Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 for internal or public VM traffic. Application Gateway is Layer 7 for web workloads — adds WAF, SSL offload, URL-path routing, and session affinity.

questions.question: Branch offices and remote workers need to reach Azure VNets securely over the internet using IPsec. The service must support BOTH site-to-site (branch-to-VNet) AND point-to-site (laptop-to-VNet) tunnel topologies. Which Azure service?
options: Azure Firewall — perimeter inspection, not a VPN tunnel terminator
Azure ExpressRoute — private dedicated link, not internet IPsec
Azure CDN — content delivery, unrelated
Azure VPN Gateway — terminates Site-to-Site, Point-to-Site, and VNet-to-VNet IPsec tunnels
questions.explanation: VPN Gateway creates encrypted tunnels over the internet: S2S (site-to-site for branch offices), P2S (point-to-site for remote workers), VNet-to-VNet. For dedicated private connections, use ExpressRoute.

questions.question: A regulated enterprise refuses to send any production traffic over the public internet between on-prem and Azure. They need a (a) DEDICATED FIBRE link via a peering partner, (b) predictable throughput (1/10/100 Gbps), (c) traffic that NEVER traverses the public internet. Which Azure service?
options: Azure CDN — content delivery edge, not a private DC↔Azure link
Azure VPN Gateway — IPsec over the public internet, doesn't bypass it
Azure ExpressRoute — dedicated private fibre from on-prem to Azure via a connectivity partner, no public-internet hops
Public-internet upgrade — not an Azure service
questions.explanation: ExpressRoute provides dedicated connectivity through a partner provider — no public internet. Offers bandwidths from 50 Mbps to 100 Gbps. Ideal for compliance, consistent performance, and large data transfers.

questions.question: An auditor asks Microsoft for documentation about (a) how customer data is handled, (b) how the cloud is operated, (c) regulatory compliance attestations (SOC, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001, GDPR). Microsoft publishes ONE central portal answering all of this. Which is it?
options: Microsoft Trust Center — central portal for security/privacy/compliance practices and regulatory attestations
Azure Security Scanner — not a real product name
A specific data-centre facility — physical, not informational
Defender for Cloud — operational posture, not Microsoft's transparency portal
questions.explanation: The Azure Trust Center (and compliance.microsoft.com) documents Microsoft's compliance certifications (ISO, SOC, GDPR, HIPAA), privacy commitments, and security practices for enterprise customers.

questions.question: A finance team migrating to cloud asks how the spending profile changes. On-prem buys hardware upfront, depreciated over 3-5 years. Cloud rents capacity per second / per request, with no upfront. Which financial-model shift does this describe?
options: Cloud uses CapEx — false; opposite
OpEx is always more expensive — context-dependent; not the definition shift
CapEx and OpEx are the same — false
Cloud shifts spending from CapEx (upfront capital hardware purchase) to OpEx (ongoing per-use consumption expense)
questions.explanation: Traditional IT: CapEx (buy servers, depreciate over time). Cloud: OpEx (pay monthly subscription/consumption). Cloud benefits: no upfront cost, scale up/down, stop paying when not needed.

questions.question: An enterprise needs to deploy a STANDARDISED Azure environment for every new project — including resource groups, ARM templates, RBAC role assignments, and Policy assignments — bundled as a VERSIONED artefact. New projects pick a version of the bundle. Which Azure service (now being superseded by Deployment Stacks)?
options: Azure Blueprints — versioned artefact bundling RGs + ARM templates + RBAC + Policy assignments
VM image library — for OS images, not environment bundles
Cost Management tool — not environment provisioning
Network diagram design tool — not a real Azure deployment artefact
questions.explanation: Azure Blueprints define a repeatable set of resources that implements and follows organizational standards. Unlike ARM templates, Blueprints track deployed resources and can be updated centrally.

questions.question: Azure exposes the SAME resource management plane through MULTIPLE clients: a browser-based GUI, a cross-platform command-line tool with `az` commands, AND a Windows + cross-platform PowerShell module with `Az.*` cmdlets. All three target Azure Resource Manager. Which statement is correct?
options: Azure CLI is Linux-only — false; it's cross-platform (Windows / macOS / Linux / Cloud Shell)
PowerShell is the fastest — performance varies; not a tooling distinction
Three tools that hit the same ARM control plane: Portal (web GUI), Azure CLI (cross-platform `az`), Azure PowerShell (cross-platform `Az.*` cmdlets)
Each tool has unique capabilities the others lack — false; they target the same ARM API surface
questions.explanation: All three management interfaces send requests to the Azure Resource Manager API. Portal: visual, good for exploration. CLI: script-friendly, cross-platform. PowerShell: powerful scripting, better for Windows admins.

questions.question: A SaaS team needs a cloud-managed service to store database connection strings, API keys, X.509 certificates, and encryption keys. The service must use HSM-backed key storage (with a paid tier), be RBAC-controlled, audit every access, and integrate with apps via AAD-backed REST/SDK. Which Azure service?
options: Azure Key Vault — managed secrets/keys/certs vault, HSM-backed Premium tier, AAD-RBAC, audit-logged
Disk encryption (ADE) — encrypts VM disks, not a generic secrets store
Database backup — separate concept
A consumer password manager — wrong audience (end-user, not service)
questions.explanation: Key Vault stores secrets (passwords, connection strings), encryption keys (HSM-backed), and certificates. Access is controlled via Azure AD and RBAC. Every access is logged for auditing.

questions.question: A FinOps team wants ONE Azure tool that: (a) shows ACTUAL spend across services / tags / accounts, (b) groups by management groups + subscriptions + resource groups, (c) sets budgets with email / Action Group alerts, (d) optionally triggers automated cost actions. Which Azure service?
options: Pre-deploy pricing calculator — pre-deploy estimates only, not actual spend visibility
Subscription-creation portal — provisioning, not cost analytics
Azure Cost Management + Billing — actual spend visibility, budget alerts, automation actions
Service Health — incident notifications, not cost
questions.explanation: Azure Cost Management + Billing lets you analyze spending by resource, tag, department, or subscription; set budgets with alert notifications; and see recommendations for reducing costs. enables budgets and alerts, shows spending trends, and helps identify cost optimization opportunities

questions.question: Each Azure resource belongs to exactly one container that defines: (a) the billing target for the resource, (b) the role-assignment scope (RBAC), (c) per-region resource limits / quotas, (d) which directory (tenant) it trusts. One Azure account can have many of these. Which Azure construct is this?
options: An Azure AD tenant — identity boundary, not the billing+quota scope
A monthly payment plan — pricing model, not a container
An Azure Subscription — billing scope + RBAC scope + quotas; one account can own many subscriptions
A Virtual Network — networking scope, not the billing+quota+RBAC scope
questions.explanation: Subscriptions are billing units in Azure. Each subscription has its own billing, limits, and RBAC. Organizations often use separate subscriptions for dev, test, and production environments.

questions.question: A SOC team adopts a Microsoft cloud-native SIEM + SOAR with: (a) ingest connectors from Azure / M365 / AWS / on-prem syslog, (b) KQL-based detection rules, (c) UEBA, (d) automated playbooks via Logic Apps. Which Azure service?
options: Azure Firewall — perimeter inspection, not SIEM
Azure VM Management — operational, not SIEM
Microsoft Sentinel — cloud-native SIEM + SOAR with connectors, KQL detection, UEBA, automated playbooks
Azure DDoS Protection — L3/L4 only, not SIEM
questions.explanation: Microsoft Sentinel collects data at cloud scale, uses ML for threat detection, provides investigation tools, and enables automated responses (playbooks). Replaces traditional on-premises SIEM.

questions.question: A FinOps team wants to attribute Azure spend to teams + environments + cost-centres without changing resource ownership or location. They want a key/value metadata system applied to resources that propagates to billing reports + Cost Management. Which Azure feature?
options: Network Security Group labels — not Azure tags
SLA tier identifiers — pricing tier, not metadata tags
Azure Resource Tags — name/value metadata on resources for organisation, cost allocation, automation, RBAC
Static IP assignments — networking, not metadata
questions.explanation: Tags (e.g., 'Environment:Production', 'Owner:TeamA') enable cost reporting by department, automated policies, lifecycle management, and resource organization across subscriptions.

questions.question: An ops team needs PERSONALISED alerts when an Azure service incident or planned maintenance affects THEIR specific subscriptions + resources (not a generic global status page). Which Azure service surfaces these targeted notifications?
options: Azure Service Health — personalised alerts for incidents, planned maintenance, and advisories scoped to your subscriptions and regions
The public Azure status page — generic global view, not subscription-specific
The Azure SLA marketing page — contractual SLA per service, not real-time health
Azure VM health metrics — VM-level only, not platform incidents
questions.explanation: Service Health provides three feeds: Service Issues (active incidents), Planned Maintenance (scheduled work), and Health Advisories. Customized to your subscriptions and regions with alert rules.

questions.question: What is the difference between Azure AD Free and Azure AD Premium?
options: Premium P1/P2 adds: Conditional Access,.
Premium is only for enterprise accounts
There is no difference
Free includes all features
questions.explanation: Azure AD Free: basic SSO, MFA for administrators. Premium P1: Conditional Access, hybrid identity. Premium P2: Identity Protection (risky sign-ins), Privileged Identity Management (just-in-time access). Identity Protection, Privileged Identity Management (PIM), self-service password reset, MFA per-user enforcement, and advanced reporting

questions.question: What is the Azure Well-Architected Framework?
options: Microsoft's guidance for designing reliable,.
An ARM template library
Azure's pricing calculator
A building design framework
questions.explanation: The Azure Well-Architected Framework provides best practices across 5 pillars to evaluate architecture quality. The Azure Advisor tool surfaces actionable recommendations aligned to these pillars. secure, efficient, and cost-effective Azure solutions across 5 pillars: Reliability, Security, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence, Performance Efficiency

questions.question: What is Azure Cognitive Services?
options: A data analytics service
A collection of AI APIs (vision,.
A database service
A security scanning tool
questions.explanation: Azure Cognitive Services provides pre-built AI capabilities via REST APIs: Computer Vision, Face, Speech-to-Text, Text Analytics, Translator, and more. No ML training required. speech, language, decision) that enable apps to see, hear, speak, understand, and decide without ML expertise

questions.question: What is Azure Machine Learning?
options: A BI reporting tool
A cloud-based platform for training,.
An AI chatbot service
A database for ML data
questions.explanation: Azure ML provides MLOps capabilities: experiment tracking, automated ML, model registry, pipelines, and deployment to real-time or batch inference endpoints. Supports Python, R, and popular ML frameworks. deploying, and managing machine learning models at scale

questions.question: An IoT solution must connect millions of devices, with: (a) device-to-cloud telemetry ingestion, (b) cloud-to-device commands, (c) per-device identity + auth, (d) device twins, (e) routing of messages to downstream Azure services. Which Azure service is the device gateway?
options: Azure Synapse — analytics, not a device gateway
Azure IoT Hub — managed bidirectional device↔cloud gateway with per-device identity + twins + routing
Azure Networking Hub — networking term, not IoT
Azure WiFi service — not a real Azure service
questions.explanation: Azure IoT Hub connects, monitors, and manages millions of IoT devices. Supports MQTT, AMQP, HTTPS. Enables device-to-cloud telemetry and cloud-to-device commands with device twin state management.

questions.question: A team wants a managed full-text + AI-enrichment search service: (a) crawl S3 / Azure Blob / DBs / Cosmos for content, (b) auto-index, (c) optional skillset of OCR + entity recognition + translation + sentiment, (d) REST + SDK query. Which Azure service?
options: Azure Monitor Log Analytics — log telemetry, not generic content search
Azure SQL Database — relational, not full-text content search across mixed sources
Azure Cognitive Search (AI Search) — managed search index with crawlers + AI enrichment + REST/SDK query
Bing Web Search — public-web search, not enterprise content
questions.explanation: Azure Cognitive Search (now Azure AI Search) provides full-text search with AI enrichment pipelines. Can index documents, images, and structured data, adding semantic search, vector search, and AI-extracted metadata.

questions.question: An analytics team wants ONE Azure platform that combines (a) MPP SQL Pools (data warehouse), (b) on-demand Apache Spark pools (big-data + ML), (c) Pipelines for ETL orchestration, (d) Studio UI for both data engineers and analysts. Which Azure service unifies these into one workspace?
options: Azure Synapse Analytics — unifies SQL Pools (DW) + Spark Pools + Data Pipelines + Studio in one workspace
Azure Cosmos DB — NoSQL, not analytics warehouse + Spark
Event Hubs — event-streaming, not analytics warehouse
Power BI alone — visualisation layer, not the warehouse + Spark workspace
questions.explanation: Azure Synapse integrates data warehousing, big data, and data integration. Dedicated SQL Pools for DW, Apache Spark for big data, integrated Pipelines for ETL, and Power BI connectivity.

questions.question: A finance team is comparing cloud deployment models. (a) Customer rents shared infra owned + operated by a CSP (multi-tenant), (b) Customer owns or rents single-tenant infra in their DC or a hosted facility, (c) Customer uses both — some workloads in (a), some in (b), interconnected. Which mapping is correct?
options: Public = CSP-managed shared; Private = single-tenant (on-prem or hosted); Hybrid = both with interconnection
Hybrid requires two CSP subscriptions — false; hybrid is on-prem + cloud, not two cloud accounts
All three are the same — false
Private is always more expensive — generally true at scale, but not the DEFINITION question
questions.explanation: Public cloud: shared, multi-tenant, Microsoft-owned. Private cloud: dedicated hardware (Azure Dedicated Host) or Azure Stack Hub on-premises. Hybrid: connects both, enabling workload portability. Private: dedicated Azure Stack or on-premises. Hybrid: combination of public Azure + on-premises/private cloud connected via VPN or ExpressRoute

questions.question: A managed-service provider (MSP) runs operations for 50 customer organisations, each in their own Azure tenant. The MSP wants ONE pane in their own tenant to manage all 50 — without creating guest accounts in each customer tenant and without context-switching. Which Azure service?
options: Azure Lighthouse — cross-tenant management plane that delegates scoped access from customer tenants to the MSP's tenant
Azure Sentinel — SIEM, narrower than cross-tenant management
Azure SDK — client library, not a management service
Azure Monitor — telemetry, not cross-tenant access delegation
questions.explanation: Azure Lighthouse provides cross-tenant management. MSPs can manage customer environments without logging into each tenant separately. Customers maintain full visibility and control over delegated access.

questions.question: An enterprise has servers in on-prem datacentres, in AWS, and in GCP. They want one Azure-portal control plane to apply Azure Policy, RBAC, Defender for Cloud posture, and Azure Monitor to ALL of them — as if they were Azure resources. Which Azure service?
options: Azure Backup — backup workloads, not multi-cloud management
An Azure wireless network — not a real management product
Azure CDN — content delivery, unrelated
Azure Arc — projects non-Azure servers / Kubernetes / databases into the Azure Resource Manager control plane
questions.explanation: Azure Arc brings Azure's management (RBAC, Policy, Monitor, Defender) to non-Azure resources: on-premises servers, Kubernetes clusters on AWS/GCP, and Azure Stack Edge. Enables consistent governance everywhere.

questions.question: A new Azure customer with no existing Azure spend wants to evaluate the platform for a month. Microsoft offers a free starter that includes $200 of credit for 30 days, free monthly amounts of popular services for 12 months, AND a catalogue of 25+ always-free services. Which offer?
options: Education-only program — narrower student offer (Azure for Students)
Azure is always free — false; only specific services are always free
Azure Free Account — $200/30-day credit + 12 months of free popular services + 25+ always-free services
Non-profit-only offer — separate Microsoft program (NfP grants)
questions.explanation: Azure Free Account: $200 credit for 30 days exploration, 12 months free for popular services (B1S VM, 5 GB Blob Storage, etc.), plus 55+ always-free services like Azure Functions (1M requests/month).

questions.question: A defence customer needs to run Azure services on-prem in their air-gapped facility (Stack Hub), on rugged edge devices (Stack Edge), and on a hyperconverged HCI rack (Stack HCI). All three share Azure's APIs / RBAC / Marketplace. What is this family called?
options: Container orchestration platform — not the Azure-on-prem family
Azure Stack family — Stack Hub (on-prem Azure), Stack Edge (edge appliance), Stack HCI (HCI rack)
An app SDK — not a hardware family
Storage tiering — not the Azure-on-prem family
questions.explanation: Azure Stack Hub: full Azure services in your datacenter for disconnected/regulatory scenarios. Stack Edge: AI-enabled appliance for edge computing. Stack HCI: hyper-converged infrastructure running Azure services locally.

questions.question: A global news site serves static assets (images, JS, CSS) to readers worldwide. The team wants edge nodes in every region caching the assets close to readers, reducing origin load and latency. Which Azure service?
options: Azure CDN — global edge cache for static + dynamic content, reduces origin load + latency
Azure SQL geo-replication — DB feature, not asset caching
Azure Load Balancer — regional L4 LB, not edge cache
Azure VPN — connectivity, unrelated to caching
questions.explanation: Azure CDN caches content (images, CSS, JS, videos) at Points of Presence (PoPs) close to users. Reduces origin server load and delivery latency. Partners: Microsoft, Verizon, Akamai (now converging to Microsoft CDN).

questions.question: An enterprise integration pattern needs: (a) durable message queues with FIFO + dead-lettering, (b) pub/sub topics with filtered subscriptions, (c) transactions across queues + topics, (d) AAD auth + private endpoints + RBAC. Which Azure messaging service?
options: Azure Service Bus — managed enterprise message broker with queues + topics + transactions + dead-letter + AAD
An on-prem hardware network bus — not an Azure service
Azure Networking — generic term, not a messaging product
Physical server connection cable — not relevant
questions.explanation: Azure Service Bus provides enterprise messaging: queues (point-to-point), topics/subscriptions (pub/sub). Supports FIFO, sessions, deferred processing, dead-letter queues, and at-least-once delivery.

questions.question: What is Azure Bot Service?
options: A virtual assistant for Azure management
A platform for building, testing.
An IoT device control service
A physical robot management system
questions.explanation: Azure Bot Service provides a framework for building conversational AI bots. Integrates with Azure Cognitive Services (LUIS/CLU for NLP, QnA Maker/Knowledge Base for FAQ). Deployed to multiple channels. deploying, and managing intelligent chatbots across multiple channels (Teams, Slack, web, Cortana)

questions.question: A device manufacturer wants a turnkey IoT-security platform: a HARDENED MCU chip with built-in roots of trust + a custom Linux-based OS + a cloud security service to issue per-device certs, manage updates, and detect threats. Which Microsoft offering covers all three?
options: A monitoring dashboard — not a hardware+OS+cloud solution
A networking protocol — not relevant
Azure Sphere — Microsoft-certified MCU + Sphere OS + Azure Sphere Security Service end-to-end IoT security
An object-storage class — unrelated
questions.explanation: Azure Sphere is Microsoft's hardware-software IoT security platform: custom MCU with security features, hardened Linux OS, and the Azure Sphere Security Service for OTA updates and certificate management.

questions.question: What is the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF)?
options: A pricing model
A collection of documentation,.
An Azure portal feature
A compliance certification
questions.explanation: CAF provides proven guidance for Azure adoption: Strategy, Plan, Ready (landing zones), Migrate, Innovate, Secure, Manage, and Govern phases. Helps organizations move to Azure systematically and reduce risk. guidance, best practices, and tools for organizations planning, implementing, and operating Azure at scale

questions.question: Dev teams need self-service Azure VMs for prototyping, with policy caps on size + count + region, automatic shutdown at 19:00 local time to control cost, reusable VM templates with checked-in artefacts, and per-user quotas. Which Azure service?
options: Azure App Service production deployment — wrong tool for ad-hoc dev VMs
CI/CD pipeline service (Azure Pipelines) — different surface
Azure Monitor — observability, not VM sandbox provisioning
Azure DevTest Labs — self-service VM sandboxes with templates, cost controls, auto-shutdown, policy caps
questions.explanation: DevTest Labs lets teams create on-demand VMs and environments from pre-approved templates with cost thresholds, auto-shutdown policies, and claiming/reclaiming capabilities — reducing dev/test spending.

questions.question: A company has 200 on-prem VMs running unchanged Windows / Linux apps. They want to migrate to Azure FAST, with minimal application change — the VMs become Azure VMs with the same OS / network / data, and refactoring is deferred for later. Which migration strategy is this?
options: Physical-server shipping — not the named strategy
Containerisation — re-architecture, opposite of minimal change
Refactor / rewrite as cloud-native — opposite of minimal change
Lift-and-shift — move on-prem VMs to Azure IaaS with minimal change; defer refactor
questions.explanation: Lift and shift (rehost) = move as-is to IaaS. Fastest migration approach. Other strategies: replatform (minor optimizations), refactor/re-architect (redesign for cloud-native), rebuild (start fresh), replace (SaaS).

questions.question: A Java team runs 25 Spring Boot microservices. They want a managed PaaS that natively understands Spring Boot: service discovery, config server, blue/green deployment, distributed tracing, autoscale, monitoring — without operating any infrastructure. Which Azure service?
options: Azure Spring Apps — managed PaaS for Spring Boot microservices: service discovery, config, blue/green, scale, monitoring
Generic testing service — not the Spring Boot PaaS
Spring-specific database — not a real Azure product
Generic Java deployment service only — too narrow
questions.explanation: Azure Spring Apps (developed with VMware/Broadcom) provides a fully managed Spring runtime. Developers focus on code; Azure manages the underlying infrastructure, networking, and service discovery.

questions.question: A security team adopts a published security guidance baseline for Azure aligned with CIS and NIST that includes prescriptive controls per service (network security, identity, data protection, logging). The baseline is free, Microsoft-published, and used to score Defender for Cloud's recommendations. What is it?
options: Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark (formerly Azure Security Benchmark) — prescriptive controls mapped to CIS, NIST, PCI-DSS; the default policy in Defender for Cloud
A penetration-testing framework — different surface (active testing, not baseline)
A third-party compliance certification — paid auditor process
A VM performance benchmark — performance not security
questions.explanation: The Azure Security Benchmark (now Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark) provides prioritized security recommendations for Azure aligned with CIS Controls and NIST SP 800-53. Used as a baseline in Defender for Cloud.

questions.question: An app dev team wants 'high-level' purpose-built AI APIs: extract structured data from invoices (Form Recognizer), detect anomalies in time-series (Metrics Advisor), summarise long documents — without training their own ML models. Which Azure AI family?
options: Generic AI APIs — too vague
Azure ML training platform — for custom model training, not purpose-built APIs
Azure Applied AI Services — purpose-built APIs (Form Recognizer, Metrics Advisor, Video Analyzer, Immersive Reader) on top of Cognitive Services
Data Labelling tool — narrow, not the AI-API family
questions.explanation: Applied AI Services are higher-level solutions built on Cognitive Services for specific business scenarios. They require less customization than building from scratch with raw Cognitive Services APIs.

questions.question: Two HA constructs in Azure: (A) groups VMs within the SAME datacentre but across distinct fault and update domains — protects from rack-level outages. (B) groups VMs across DIFFERENT physically-isolated facilities with independent power and network — protects from facility-level outages. Which mapping?
options: They are identical — false
Availability Sets span multiple regions — false; Sets are within ONE datacentre
Availability Set = fault+update domains in one DC; Availability Zone = separate facilities within a Region
Zones are older than Sets — reversed; Zones are newer
questions.explanation: Availability Sets (2+ VMs): 99.95% SLA — distributes VMs across fault domains (separate racks) and update domains. Availability Zones (3 zones in a region): 99.99% SLA — separate buildings, better protection.

questions.question: A research team needs to run thousands of parallel compute jobs (Monte-Carlo, batch rendering, genomics) with auto-scaled VM pools, queue-of-tasks dispatch, support for low-priority spot nodes, and result aggregation. Which Azure service?
options: Azure Batch — managed HPC/parallel-job service: auto-scaled VM pools + task queues + spot nodes + result aggregation
ETL batch service (Data Factory) — data pipelines, not generic HPC
Messaging batch (Service Bus) — messaging, not compute jobs
DB batch processing — relational, not generic HPC
questions.explanation: Azure Batch handles the infrastructure for HPC and batch jobs: provision compute pools, schedule jobs, retry failed tasks. Pay for VMs used. Ideal for 3D rendering, simulation, genomics, financial modeling.

questions.question: An admin compares Managed vs Unmanaged disks in Azure. Managed: Azure handles the storage-account layer (no customer-visible storage account, no per-account IOPS/throughput limit to manage). Unmanaged: customer owns the storage accounts hosting the VHDs and the 20k-IOPS-per-account ceiling. Which statement?
options: Managed is more expensive — false; pricing similar; Managed is the recommended default
Managed = Azure owns the storage-account layer (no per-account limits to plan); Unmanaged = customer-managed storage accounts and limits
Unmanaged is more reliable — false; Managed has built-in availability set integration and is recommended
They are identical — false
questions.explanation: Azure Managed Disks handle storage account management, capacity planning, and redundancy automatically. Support encryption, backup (snapshots, Azure Backup), and role-based access. Types: Ultra Disk, Premium SSD, Standard SSD, Standard HDD. replication, and redundancy automatically. Unmanaged Disks: you manage storage accounts manually (legacy). Managed Disks is the recommended approach for all new workloads

questions.question: An Azure Policy assignment with effect=Deny blocks resource creation that violates the rule. A different effect, AUDIT, only logs non-compliance without blocking. Which describes the Deny effect specifically?
options: Notifies admins only — that's a separate alerting mechanism, not Deny
Prevents non-compliant resource deployment at create-time — Audit reports, Deny BLOCKS
Deletes existing non-compliant resources — Deny applies at create-time, not retro-delete
Logs without blocking — that's Audit, not Deny
questions.explanation: Azure Policy effects: Deny (block), Audit (log), Append (add fields), Modify (alter properties), DeployIfNotExists (deploy remediation), AuditIfNotExists (audit if related resource missing). Deny is the most restrictive.

questions.question: An architect runs an evaluation of an existing workload against the 5 Well-Architected pillars (Reliability, Security, Cost Optimisation, Operational Excellence, Performance Efficiency) and gets a scored report + recommendations. The tool is free and lives in the Azure portal. Which is it?
options: A pricing-review consult — not the assessment tool
Azure Well-Architected Review — free self-assessment in the Azure portal scoring a workload against the 5 pillars
Azure audit service — not a real Azure product name
A formal compliance certification — paid auditor process, not a self-assessment
questions.explanation: The Well-Architected Review asks 50+ questions about your workload across the 5 pillars. Results show your score per pillar and recommendations prioritized by impact. Helps identify architectural risks and improvement areas.

questions.question: A platform team wants to give developers self-service Azure VMs for testing with: (a) pre-built images, (b) auto-shutdown to control cost, (c) per-user policy caps, (d) checked-in artefacts auto-applied. Which Azure service?
options: Azure DevTest Labs — self-service VM sandboxes with templates, cost controls, auto-shutdown, policy
Azure DevOps Pipelines — CI/CD, not VM sandbox provisioning
Azure Load Testing — performance testing, not VM sandboxes
A testing framework — generic, not the Azure service
questions.explanation: DevTest Labs lets teams spin up dev/test environments quickly using templates. Features: auto-shutdown policies to save costs, spending caps, claimable VMs, artifact library (install software automatically).

questions.question: An admin compares two foundational Azure concepts: (A) a dedicated identity / directory instance (Azure AD instance) representing a single organisation — the identity boundary; (B) a billing + management scope that holds resources, billed and quota-limited as a unit. Many Bs can belong to one A. Which is which?
options: Tenant = the Azure AD instance / identity boundary; Subscription = the billing + resource scope within a tenant
Tenant and Subscription are identical — false
Each subscription has its own Azure AD — false; many subscriptions share one tenant
Subscription is bigger than tenant — reversed; tenant contains many subscriptions
questions.explanation: Azure AD Tenant: created when your organization signs up for Azure — owns user identities. Subscription: billing container for resources, associated with one tenant. Multiple subscriptions can share one tenant (common for large organizations).

questions.question: Azure Monitor exposes telemetry in two distinct stores: (A) NUMERIC, time-series, lightweight data (CPU %, mem %, network bytes) at 1-minute granularity, queried in Metrics Explorer; (B) RICH structured records (request traces, audit, performance counters) stored in Log Analytics, queried with KQL. Which mapping?
options: They are identical — false
Metrics = numeric time-series queried in Metrics Explorer; Logs = rich structured records in Log Analytics queried via KQL
Metrics use KQL — false; Logs use KQL
Logs retained for less time than Metrics — false; Logs retention is configurable (longer for paid tiers)
questions.explanation: Metrics: lightweight, fast, great for real-time alerts and dashboards. Logs (Log Analytics): rich query capability with KQL, long retention, can combine data from many sources (VMs, apps, security, network). requests/sec) stored for 93 days by default, near real-time, optimized for dashboards and alerts. Logs: structured/unstructured event data in Log Analytics workspace, queried with KQL

questions.question: A finance team commits to a STEADY 3-year workload of a specific VM size in a specific region. In exchange for the upfront commitment, Microsoft offers up to ~72% discount versus pay-as-you-go. The discount applies automatically as the running VMs match the commitment. Which Azure pricing model?
options: Locking in IP addresses — not a pricing model
Reserved VM Instances (1 or 3-yr commitment to a VM size+region, up to ~72% off PAYG)
Reserving VM names — not a pricing model
Reserving storage — different model (storage reservations exist separately)
questions.explanation: Reserved VM Instances (RIs) offer significant cost savings for steady workloads: Standard RI (fixed size), Convertible RI (can change size/series). Commitment: 1yr (~40% off) or 3yr (~72% off). Can be exchanged or sold.

questions.question: In the Azure shared-responsibility model for IaaS, AZURE handles physical hardware, hypervisor, networking, and facilities. The CUSTOMER handles the guest OS, runtime, middleware, and application+data. The compute primitive is a VM the customer provisions. Which cloud service model is this?
options: PaaS — Azure manages OS and runtime; customer manages app+data only
FaaS — Azure manages everything except the function code
SaaS — Azure manages the entire app stack; customer just configures and uses
IaaS — Azure provides virtualised hardware (VMs/disks/network); customer manages guest OS, runtime, app, data
questions.explanation: IaaS: rent compute, network, storage infrastructure. You manage: OS patches, runtime, applications. Examples: Azure VMs, Virtual Networks, Azure Storage. Compare PaaS (Azure manages OS too) and SaaS (managed entirely). networking, storage). Customer manages: OS, middleware, runtime, data, applications. Example: Azure Virtual Machines

questions.question: A VM in a VNet needs to reach an Azure Storage account so that (a) traffic goes via a PRIVATE IP from the VNet, (b) traffic NEVER crosses the public internet, (c) the storage account's public endpoint can be DISABLED entirely. Which Azure feature?
options: A public IP — opposite of private
Private Endpoint — gives the PaaS service a NIC with a private IP in the VNet; public endpoint can be disabled
VPN gateway endpoint — for cross-network IPsec, not in-VNet PaaS access
ExpressRoute connection point — for DC-to-Azure, not in-VNet PaaS access
questions.explanation: Private Endpoints create a NIC in your VNet for an Azure service. DNS resolves the service name to the private IP. Traffic from your VNet never leaves the Azure network. Enables strict private connectivity for compliance.

questions.question: What is the Azure Free Account?
options: Azure services are always free
Only one month of free services
12 months of popular services free.
Requires a credit card but never charged
questions.explanation: Azure Free Account: $200 credit for 30 days (explore any service), 12 months free for popular services (VMs, Blob, SQL), and permanently free tiers for services like Functions (1M executions/month), Cosmos DB (400 RU/s), and others. $200 credit for 30 days to explore all services, and 55+ always-free services (Functions, Blob Storage, Cosmos DB, SQL Database at limited tiers)

questions.question: An ops team must patch Azure VMs + Azure-Arc-enabled on-prem servers on a unified schedule, with compliance reporting, classification-based selection (Critical / Security), and reboot orchestration. Which Azure service?
options: A Windows Update service alone — Windows only, not on-prem servers or Arc
Azure Update Manager — unified update/patch governance for Azure VMs + Arc-enabled on-prem + multi-cloud servers
Firmware update tool — hardware only, not OS patches
Azure AD update — identity service, not OS patching
questions.explanation: Azure Update Manager (formerly Update Management in Automation) provides a centralized dashboard for update compliance and deployment across Windows/Linux VMs. Supports Azure VMs, Arc-enabled servers, and on-premises.

questions.question: A compliance officer wants ONE unified portal covering (a) compliance posture across regulations (Compliance Manager), (b) sensitive-data discovery + classification + labels (Information Protection), (c) DLP rules across email + endpoints + cloud apps, (d) eDiscovery + insider-risk + records management. Which Microsoft portal?
options: Microsoft Defender for Cloud — security posture, narrower than compliance + DLP + eDiscovery
Azure Monitor — telemetry, not compliance
Microsoft Purview compliance portal — unified compliance / data governance / DLP / eDiscovery / insider-risk
Azure Data Catalog only — narrow, just data catalog
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview combines compliance features: Compliance Manager (regulatory compliance score and tracking), Information Protection (classify/label data), DLP (prevent data leaks), eDiscovery (legal holds), Insider Risk Management.

questions.question: A SecOps team wants ONE unified platform on the security side of Azure that provides: (a) Secure Score across subscriptions, (b) threat detection per workload (VM, SQL, Storage, K8s), (c) regulatory compliance dashboards, (d) extends to AWS / GCP / on-prem via Azure Arc. Which Azure service?
options: Endpoint antivirus per VM — agent on individual VMs, narrower than the multi-workload posture platform
Identity-only security service (Azure AD Identity Protection) — narrower than multi-workload posture
Microsoft Defender for Cloud (Azure Security Center) — unified posture + threat protection across Azure / multi-cloud / on-prem with Secure Score and compliance dashboards
Standalone firewall service — narrower than posture + threat + compliance
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud (formerly Security Center + Azure Defender): Free tier provides Secure Score and basic recommendations. Paid tier adds threat protection for servers, storage, SQL, containers, Key Vault, and more.

questions.question: Two CLI tools both manage Azure resources: (A) Bash-friendly, `az` verb-noun commands, cross-platform (Windows/macOS/Linux), JSON output, designed for Linux + scripts. (B) PowerShell cmdlets `Az.*`, object-pipeline-friendly, cross-platform (PS 7), familiar for Windows-admin shops. Which mapping?
options: CLI is Linux-only — false; Azure CLI is cross-platform
They are identical — false; different syntax, output format, scripting style
Azure CLI (`az`, cross-platform, Bash-friendly, JSON output); Azure PowerShell (`Az.*` cmdlets, cross-platform PS 7, object-pipeline)
PowerShell doesn't support Azure — false; Azure PowerShell is fully supported
questions.explanation: Azure CLI: az commands, great for Bash scripts and Linux/Mac, simple syntax. Azure PowerShell: Az cmdlets, powerful for Windows scripting, integrates with Windows automation. Both are cross-platform and call the same ARM API.

questions.question: What is Azure Arc?
options: A CDN service
Extends Azure management to on-premises,.
A backup service
An Azure networking service
questions.explanation: Azure Arc registers non-Azure resources (on-premises VMs, AWS/GCP VMs, Kubernetes clusters) in Azure as Arc-enabled resources. Enables consistent governance, security, and management across environments using Azure tools. multi-cloud, and edge resources — enabling Azure Policy, RBAC, Defender for Cloud, and Azure Monitor on servers/Kubernetes clusters outside Azure

questions.question: An admin needs a catalogue of certified software (VMs, containers, SaaS) and consulting services from Microsoft + partners, with billing through their existing Azure subscription invoice. Which Azure portal?
options: An Azure training portal — Microsoft Learn, not a catalogue of software for sale
An Azure shopping site for hardware — not a real Microsoft portal
Azure Marketplace — certified applications + services + SaaS + professional services from Microsoft and partners, billed via Azure invoice
Azure Support — ticketing, not a software catalogue
questions.explanation: Azure Marketplace offers: VM images (pre-configured with software like SAP, Oracle, Palo Alto), SaaS applications, development tools, security solutions, and professional services. Some are free, others have per-hour or per-seat pricing.

questions.question: A platform team needs a PRIVATE container registry hosted on Azure: OCI-compliant, AAD-auth, geo-replicated, content-trust signing, helm-chart support, AKS-native pull. Which Azure service?
options: Container monitoring service — not a registry
Public image repository (e.g., Docker Hub) — public, not private
Azure Container Registry (ACR) — private OCI registry with AAD, geo-replication, content trust, helm support, AKS-native
Container orchestrator (AKS) — runs workloads, doesn't store images
questions.explanation: ACR is Azure's private container registry. Build and push images, sign them for security, use geo-replication for global distribution. Integrates with CI/CD (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions) and deploys to AKS, ACI, App Service.

questions.question: What is the Azure Shared Responsibility Model for Platform as a Service (PaaS)?
options: Same as IaaS responsibility split
Azure manages: infrastructure.
Customer manages everything
Azure manages applications too
questions.explanation: PaaS responsibility: Azure handles physical security, hardware, OS, runtime/platform patching. You handle: application code, data, access management, client-side security. Middle ground between IaaS (manage OS) and SaaS (manage nothing). OS, platform runtime, and middleware. Customer manages: applications, data, user access, and some network configurations. Example: Azure App Service, Azure SQL Database

questions.question: Your organization was using 'Azure Active Directory' for identity and access management. You notice Microsoft now refers to it by a new name in the portal and documentation. What is the current official name of this service?
options: Microsoft Entra ID
Azure AD Premium
Microsoft 365 Identity
Azure Identity Manager
questions.explanation: In 2023, Microsoft rebranded Azure Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID as part of the broader Microsoft Entra product family. The service capabilities (tenants, users, groups, Conditional Access, MFA) are unchanged — only the name and logos were updated.

questions.question: A cloud administrator wants an AI-powered assistant integrated directly into the Azure portal to help design architectures, write CLI commands, query resource health, and troubleshoot issues using natural language. Which Microsoft service provides this capability?
options: Microsoft Copilot in Azure
Azure Monitor Insights
Azure Advisor
Azure Resource Explorer
questions.explanation: Microsoft Copilot in Azure is an AI assistant embedded in the Azure portal that helps users design, operate, optimize, and troubleshoot Azure resources through natural-language prompts. Advisor gives recommendations but not conversational AI.

questions.question: A team needs to deploy GPT-4 and other OpenAI models in Azure with enterprise features such as private networking, content filtering, responsible AI controls, and regional data residency. Which Azure service should they use?
options: Azure Bot Service
Azure Machine Learning Studio
Azure OpenAI Service (Azure AI Foundry)
Azure Cognitive Search
questions.explanation: Azure OpenAI Service, now part of Azure AI Foundry, provides managed access to OpenAI models (GPT-4, GPT-4o, DALL-E, Whisper, embeddings) with Azure enterprise features: private endpoints, content filters, customer-managed keys, and regional deployments.

questions.question: A DevOps team wants a fully managed Grafana service in Azure to visualize metrics from Azure Monitor, Prometheus, and other data sources, with Entra ID authentication and workspace-level RBAC. Which service should they use?
options: Power BI Embedded
Azure Data Explorer Dashboards
Azure Monitor Workbooks
Azure Managed Grafana
questions.explanation: Azure Managed Grafana is a fully managed service that runs Grafana Enterprise in Azure. It integrates natively with Azure Monitor, supports Entra ID SSO, and provides workspace-level role assignments so teams can share dashboards securely.

questions.question: An enterprise is planning a large-scale migration to Azure and wants a prescriptive framework that covers strategy, planning, readiness, adoption, governance, and management — including pre-built 'landing zones' with baseline networking, identity, and security controls. Which Microsoft resource provides this?
options: Azure Well-Architected Framework
Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) with Azure Landing Zones
Azure Migrate
Microsoft Assessment and Planning Toolkit
questions.explanation: The Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) is Microsoft's end-to-end guidance for cloud adoption. Azure Landing Zones are CAF's reference implementations that provide a pre-configured, scalable foundation (management groups, policies, networking, identity) ready for workloads.

questions.question: Finance asks you to track Azure spending, set alert thresholds per subscription, and receive automatic recommendations to buy Reserved Instances or Savings Plans to lower costs. Which combination of Azure tools should you use?
options: Azure Policy with cost tags
Microsoft Cost Management with budgets,.
Azure Pricing Calculator only
Azure Monitor metrics alerts on billing data
questions.explanation: Microsoft Cost Management provides cost analysis, budgets with alert thresholds, and forecasting. Azure Advisor's Cost category surfaces right-sizing, Reserved Instance, and Savings Plan recommendations based on usage patterns. plus Azure Advisor cost recommendations

questions.question: A company runs Windows and Linux servers on-premises plus Kubernetes clusters in AWS. They want to manage all of these from the Azure portal using Azure Policy, tag governance, and Defender for Cloud — without migrating the workloads. Which Azure service enables this?
options: Azure Site Recovery
Azure Stack HCI
Azure Migrate
Azure Arc
questions.explanation: Azure Arc extends Azure's control plane to resources outside Azure — servers, Kubernetes clusters, and data services on-premises or in other clouds. Once onboarded, they appear as Azure resources and can be governed by Azure Policy, RBAC, Defender for Cloud, and Azure Monitor.

questions.question: A healthcare customer must process encrypted data in memory so that not even the cloud provider or hypervisor admin can read it during computation. Which Azure capability addresses this requirement?
options: Azure Disk Encryption
Azure Confidential Computing using Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs)
Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
Azure Storage Service Encryption
questions.explanation: Azure Confidential Computing protects data in use by running workloads inside hardware-based Trusted Execution Environments (such as Intel SGX or AMD SEV-SNP). Data remains encrypted in memory and is inaccessible even to host administrators or the hypervisor.

questions.question: A data governance team needs a unified catalog that discovers, classifies, and tracks the lineage of data assets across Azure, on-premises SQL, AWS S3, and Power BI. Which service provides this?
options: Microsoft Purview Data Governance
Azure Data Factory
Azure Data Catalog (classic)
Azure Synapse Analytics
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview (formerly Azure Purview / Azure Data Catalog) is a unified data governance solution providing data discovery, automated classification, lineage tracking, and sensitivity labeling across multi-cloud and on-premises data estates.

questions.question: A developer wants to instrument a microservices application using the vendor-neutral OpenTelemetry standard and send traces, metrics, and logs to an Azure observability service with APM features like dependency maps and live metrics. Which service should they use?
options: Azure Log Analytics only
Azure Monitor Application Insights (with OpenTelemetry distro)
Azure Network Watcher
Azure Service Map
questions.explanation: Azure Monitor Application Insights supports the OpenTelemetry standard via Microsoft's OpenTelemetry Distro, letting developers use vendor-neutral instrumentation while getting Application Insights features: application map, live metrics, failures, and end-to-end transaction diagnostics.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about Azure Availability Zones are TRUE?
options: Each Availability Zone is a physically separate datacenter within an Azure region
Resources deployed across zones in the same region are billed for inter-region data transfer
Zone-redundant services automatically replicate across multiple zones in the region
Availability Zones are available in every Azure region
questions.explanation: AZs are physically separate datacenters with independent power/network within one region. Zone-redundant services (e.g., zone-redundant Storage, SQL Premium, AKS) replicate across zones automatically. Inter-zone traffic in the same region is intra-region (not inter-region) bandwidth. Not every region has AZs — many secondary regions do not.
